source: NCERT Class X, India and the Contemporary World II, History Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Before the Factory — Proto-industrialisation
points: **Proto-industrialisation** = large-scale industrial production for an international market **before factories**, done in the **countryside** by peasants/artisans working from home for merchants.
Merchants supplied money and raw material; the system linked towns (merchants) and villages (producers).
This preceded the factory-based **Industrial Revolution**.

sections.heading: 2. The Coming of the Factory
points: The first factories in **England** came up by the **1730s**; the **cotton industry** boomed.
Inventions: **Richard Arkwright's cotton mill**; the **spinning jenny (Hargreaves)**; the **steam engine (James Watt)** powered machines.
Factories brought together workers, machines and supervision under one roof.
But **hand labour** did not vanish; industrialisation was **slow and uneven**.

sections.heading: 3. Industrialisation in the Colonies (India)
points: Before British rule, India was the **world's leading exporter of cotton textiles**; ports like **Surat, Masulipatnam, Hoogly** flourished.
British policies **destroyed Indian handicrafts** (deindustrialisation): imported **Manchester cloth** flooded India; Indian weavers lost markets and income.
**Indian factories** rose late (from the 1850s): the first **cotton mill in Bombay (1854)** and **jute mills in Bengal**; industrialists like **Dwarkanath Tagore, Jamsetji Tata**.
**Marwari and Parsi** businessmen invested; Indian entrepreneurs faced British competition and controls.

sections.heading: 4. Workers and Advertising
points: Factory workers faced **long hours, low wages and insecure jobs**; a surplus of labour kept wages down.
**Advertising** (labels, calendars, images of gods/kings) was used to sell goods and build markets — 'Made in Manchester' labels for cloth sold in India.
Industrialisation transformed society but with great hardship for workers.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Proto-industrialisation = production for market before factories (rural, home-based, for merchants).
England: factories by 1730s; cotton boom; spinning jenny (Hargreaves), steam engine (James Watt).
India = world's leading cotton textile exporter before British rule; British policy → deindustrialisation.
First Indian cotton mill = Bombay (1854); jute mills in Bengal; Tata, Dwarkanath Tagore.
Advertising built markets ('Made in Manchester' labels).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Proto-industrialisation** was **before** the factory system (rural, merchant-controlled).
The **steam engine** is linked to **James Watt**; the **spinning jenny** to **Hargreaves**.
British rule caused **deindustrialisation** of India (ruined handloom weavers).
The first Indian **cotton mill** came up in **Bombay (1854)**.
